verdict.rationale: Highnote's collaborative authorization is a first-party feature that lets your own business logic approve or decline transactions in real time, which covers the core of the story. The evidence describes it only in a single sentence: it says nothing about how the decision endpoint is called, what the response time budget is, or what happens on timeout. Missing for 10: endpoint/request-response mechanics for the auth decision, documented network time budget, documented timeout fallback (default approve/decline) that the developer controls, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can approve or decline each authorization in real time — a webhook or auth-stream endpoint my code answers inside the network's time budget, with a documented timeout fallback I control

citations.quote: Collaborative authorization lets you approve or decline transactions in real time based on your business logic.
